title: Ray Gun no. 12, “The LA episode”
lede: A Ray Gun issue from the turn of 1993–94, with Deborah Harry interviewing L7 on the cover and headlines inside that are scattered, doubled, blurred, and sprayed.
summary: Green masthead bar over L7, scattered outline letters over body text, and a blurred, doubled “Mazzy Star” headline with yellow spray. David Carson, Ray Gun no. 12.

source.label: Display Graphic Design Collection: Ray Gun, No. 12

evidence.note: Inspected five photographs (1600 × 1279 each) of one copy offered by Display in scratchpad copies: the cover and four interior spreads. The copy has no collection number. Not stored.

styles.note: Clear example: headlines are scattered, blurred, doubled, and sprayed over body text, while the cover stays comparatively plain.

context: Display lists the issue as no. 12, 10 × 12 inches, 108 pages, art direction by David Carson, with L7 interviewed by Deborah Harry, and features on Mazzy Star, Redd Kross, Moby, and Yo La Tengo. [Display](https://bookstore.thisisdisplay.org/products/ray-gun-no-12-december-january-1993-david-carson).
Wikipedia’s issue list dates no. 12 to December 1993/January 1994, with L7 on the cover. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Gun_(magazine)).
observed: The cover is a full-bleed colour photograph of L7 with a bright green masthead bar reading “R AYGUN,” in heavy black sans-serif with an odd gap and a trailing comma.
Cover lines are a condensed sans-serif in white capitals, right-aligned in a narrow column.
The Bad Religion spread scatters large serif capitals, some in outline, across a brown duotone band photograph and over the body text; a brown splash surrounds one letter.
Pull-quote lines are set in several sizes and faces and overlap the text columns.
The Mazzy Star headline is blurred, doubled, and scratched, repeated across both pages, with yellow spray-paint marks over the body text.
The Mazzy Star body text is an italic serif set in a tilted, bending column; the photograph has a rough black border.
The Redd Kross opener uses a spiky decorative serif for the headline and byline over a red duotone photograph of sneakers.
interpretation: This issue shows how grunge damage is concentrated in headlines and ornaments. Body text stays set in conventional serifs and a typewriter face, even when it is tilted or overlapped.
borrow: Repeat a headline twice with a slight offset and blur, as a misregistered print.
Scatter the letters of one heading across a spread in mixed outline and solid capitals.
Add one spray or stain mark in a muted accent colour over body text, not over the headline.

rights.statement: No image is stored. David Carson is living, so the design is in copyright. Photographs by their sources.
